description: Tiny, zero-dependency Either/Result library for TypeScript using generator-based do-notation, typed async cancellation, scoped child work, stream helpers, Standard Schema integration, and an optional build-time transform.
rules: The package name on npm is `@big-time/yeet`. Import from it directly; it is ESM-only with zero runtime dependencies.
Use `@big-time/yeet` for the core API and `@big-time/yeet/stream` for stream/byte helpers. Do not import stream helpers from the root.
yeet has NO method-chain API. Never generate `.map`, `.flatMap`, `.andThen`, `.mapErr`, `.orElse`, or `.pipe`. Compose computations with `either(function* () { ... })` and `yield*`.
Inside an `either` generator, `yield*` an Either to unwrap a `Right` to its value; a yielded `Left` short-circuits the enclosing runner and becomes its result.

For a typed early exit use `return raise(error)`. `raise` is the first parameter of the generator function passed to `either()`, or destructure it from the `RaiseContext`: `either(function* ({ raise }) { ... })`.
Do not annotate the error type. It is inferred from the Lefts you `yield*` and the values you `raise`. Use `as const` for narrow string-literal errors, e.g. `return raise('Inactive' as const)`.

Async: write `const x = yield* await fn()` where `fn` returns `Promise<Either<...>>`. Wrap raw promises or throwing initializers with `raise(promise)` or `raise(fn)` so rejections and synchronous throws become `Left<Rejected>` instead of escaping as exceptions.

To make an async run cancellable, pass an `AbortSignal` as the first argument: `either(signal, async function* ({ signal }) { ... })`. On abort the result is `Left<Aborted>`. Pass the same signal to underlying I/O; cancellation is cooperative.

The first callback argument is a callable `RaiseContext`: prefer `async function* ({ raise, signal })` when both are needed, or `async function* ({ signal })` when only cancellation/scoped child work is needed. The same enriched signal is also passed as the callback's second argument for compatibility.

Inside async `either`, the injected `signal` is a `ScopeSignal`: it is an `AbortSignal` plus `fork(task)`, `forkAll(tasks)`, `forkFirst(tasks)`, `forkRace(tasks)`, and `forkEach(items, options, task)`. Each scoped task receives a child `ScopeSignal` and returns an `Either` or `Promise<Either>`.
Use `signal.fork(task)` for named child work tied to the generator lifetime. If the parent returns, short-circuits, throws, aborts, or closes normally, outstanding children are aborted and awaited.
Use `yield* await signal.forkAll([...])` for signal-aware batches. It starts all child tasks, preserves tuple order, and cancels siblings on the first `Left` or rejection.

Use `yield* await signal.forkFirst([...])` for concurrent first success. It starts every task, records candidate `Left` / `Rejected` failures while siblings continue, returns the first `Right`, and aborts unfinished candidates with `siblingSettled()`. If every candidate fails, it returns a position-preserving error tuple in input order; an empty input returns `Left([])`.

Use `yield* await signal.forkRace([...])` when the first typed child outcome wins. A winning `Right` aborts losers with `siblingSettled()` (`{ _tag: 'SiblingSettled' }`) without poisoning the enclosing `either`; a winning `Left` aborts losers and short-circuits.

Use `signal.forkEach(items, { concurrency }, task)` for lazy bounded work over an `Iterable` or `AsyncIterable`. It yields `{ item, index, result: Exit<E, A> }` in settlement order. Individual task failures are data: `yield* result` to fail fast, or inspect and continue.

Breaking a `forkEach` loop, calling `.return()`, or async-disposing its iterator closes the source, aborts unfinished children with `forkEachStopped()` (`{ _tag: 'ForkEachStopped' }`), and awaits teardown. It keeps active tasks plus buffered completions within `concurrency` and allows one outstanding source pull. Source-iterator failures become scoped `Left<Rejected>` failures.

If sibling teardown rejects while a scope is already unwinding, the primary failure remains primary and cleanup rejections are attached as `Suppressed` Exit-error data. If a `forkFirst` or `forkRace` `Right` wins but a loser rejects during abort cleanup, the operation returns `Left<Rejected>`.

Inside scoped child tasks, do not return a custom `Left<Cancelled>` solely because `signal.aborted`; it widens task error unions and losing tasks are discarded. Honor the signal and let yeet surface `Aborted` / `SiblingSettled` cancellation data.

Scoped async outcomes are represented by `Exit<E, A>`, equivalent to `Either<E | Aborted | Rejected | Suppressed, A>`. Use `ExitError`, `ScopeTaskError`, `ScopeTaskErrors`, `ScopeTaskValue`, and `ScopeTaskValues` when spelling scoped helper types.

Choose the runner by intent: `either` stops on the first Left; `validate` runs every check and collects all errors as `Left<E[]>` using the injected `check` helper; `firstOf` returns the first `Right`; `collect`/`collectAll` partition into `{ values, errors }` without short-circuiting; root `all` runs independent inputs concurrently and returns the first Left by input order or a tuple of successes.

Use `raise.capture(work)` for a local outcome boundary. Existing Eithers pass through by identity; raw successes become Right; returned Eithers are flattened; synchronous throws and promise rejections become `Left<Rejected>`. Inspect the result directly and only `yield*` it when you deliberately want to propagate it.
Inspect a result with `isLeft(x)` / `isRight(x)` or by checking `x._tag === 'Left'`.
Use `ensure(cond, onFail)` and `ensureNotNull(value, onNull)` for inline guard checks; `yield*` them to short-circuit with a Left on failure.

Stream helpers live at `@big-time/yeet/stream`: `bytes`, `text`, and `json` read bounded byte sources into one `Promise<Either<Aborted | StreamError, ...>>`; `chunks`, `lines`, `ndjson`, and `sse` are async iterables of `Either`; `collectText` and `consume` drain streams without per-success `Right` allocations.

For stream helpers, use size guards (`maxBytes`, `maxChars`, `maxLineBytes`) and pass `signal` through. Use `for await (const next of ndjson(source, { signal })) { const item = yield* next }` for structured streams inside `either`.
Malformed NDJSON yields `Left<ParseError>` per bad line and continues if the consumer keeps iterating. Byte limits, line limits, invalid chunks, and decode failures are stream-fatal.

Breaking a `chunks` / `lines` / `ndjson` / `sse` loop, or returning `Left` from `consume(..., { each })`, cancels the underlying `ReadableStream`. Known stop reasons are passed to `cancel(reason)`: abort `signal.reason`, external error cause, or the fatal stream error.

Serialize with `toJSON()` / `JSON.stringify`. Rehydrate trusted serialized values with `fromJSON`. For untrusted JSON, validate with `eitherSchema` / `serializedEitherSchema`, passing any Standard Schema validator (Zod, Valibot, ArkType, TypeBox); yeet imports none of them and only checks for `~standard`.

For scoped outcomes over the wire, use `exitErrorSchema`, `serializedExitSchema`, and `exitSchema`. Without a domain `error` schema, Exit schemas accept only yeet's built-in `Aborted` and `Rejected` payloads; add `reason` or `cause` schemas for tighter validation.
Do not use `this` or `arguments` inside an `either` generator.

Optional performance step: the unplugin at `@big-time/yeet/unplugin` (`/vite`, `/webpack`, `/rollup`, `/esbuild`, `/rspack`, `/bun`) lowers supported `either`/`validate`/`firstOf`/`collect` generators to plain branches at build time. It is a pure optimization and changes no behavior; code runs correctly without it.

Inside a lowered `either`, direct `right`, `left`, `ensure`, and `ensureNotNull` steps are fused so their intermediate Either is never allocated. `raise.capture(...)` is also supported as a local outcome boundary. Immutable `const` aliases initialized by Either-producing calls and `{ raise }` / `{ raise: fail }` callback parameters are supported. Shadowed helpers, mutable aliases, and scoped `{ signal }` contexts stay on the runtime path.

The optimizer can also lower non-abortable stream compositions such as `yield* await json(body)`, `yield* await collectText(stream)`, and `yield* next` where `next` is a const item from yeet `ndjson`/`sse`/`lines`/`chunks`. Abortable `either(signal, ...)` stays on the runtime driver.
